:::{#cor-conditional-as-or}
#### A conditional without the arrow

For [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $Q$,

$$
(P \Rightarrow Q) \equiv (\neg P \lor Q).
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

1. By [double negation](#thm-double-negation),
   $P \Rightarrow Q \equiv \neg \neg (P \Rightarrow Q)$.
2. By [negating a conditional](#thm-negate-conditional)
   and [replacing a part by an equivalent part](#thm-substitution-logic),
   $\neg \neg (P \Rightarrow Q) \equiv \neg (P \land \neg Q)$.
3. By the first of [De Morgan's laws](#thm-de-morgan-logic),
   $\neg (P \land \neg Q) \equiv \neg P \lor \neg \neg Q$.
4. By double negation and replacing a part by an equivalent part again,
   $\neg P \lor \neg \neg Q \equiv \neg P \lor Q$.

:::

:::
